meta.title: ClamStop: close the lid and your MacBook sleeps
meta.description: Open source menu bar app for macOS: closing the lid puts your MacBook to sleep, even with an external display connected, then hibernates it after a delay.
meta.og_alt: ClamStop: close the lid, and your Mac sleeps.
og.tagline: Close the lid, and your Mac sleeps.
nav.label: Main
hero.title: Close the lid. Your Mac goes to sleep.
hero.lead: ClamStop is a menu bar app that puts a MacBook to sleep when its lid closes, even with an external display connected, then hibernates it after the delay you choose.
hero.requirements: macOS 14 Sonoma or later · Apple silicon and Intel · Open source (MIT)
why.title: Why ClamStop?
why.problem: When a MacBook is connected to an external display, macOS keeps it awake after the lid closes (clamshell mode). Since macOS 26 Tahoe, there is no longer a setting to turn this off.
why.solution: With ClamStop, closing the lid always puts the Mac to sleep, as it does when nothing is connected. Open the lid or press a key to wake it.
why.hibernation: After the chosen delay, the Mac hibernates: the content of its memory is saved to disk and it stops drawing power, which spares the battery. Waking up then takes a few seconds longer.
shot.settings.alt: ClamStop settings window: sleep when the lid closes is on, hibernation after 5 minutes, audio paused while the Mac sleeps, icon shown in the menu bar, and the background service running.
shot.settings.caption: All the settings fit in one window.
shot.menu.alt: ClamStop menu in the menu bar: current status, Sleep When the Lid Closes, Settings and Quit ClamStop.
shot.menu.caption: Turn it on or off from the menu bar.
features.title: Features
features.clamshell.title: Sleep in clamshell mode too
features.clamshell.text: Closing the lid puts the Mac to sleep, whether or not a display, keyboard or power adapter is connected.
features.assertions.title: Apps cannot keep it awake
features.assertions.text: The Mac sleeps on lid close even while audio plays or an app asks it to stay awake. No app is force-quit.
features.hibernate.title: Delayed hibernation
features.hibernate.text: Hibernate immediately, after 5 minutes to 4 hours of sleep, or never. A hibernating Mac draws no power from its battery.
features.audio.title: Quiet while asleep
features.audio.text: ClamStop can pause playback when the lid closes and resume it when you open the lid.
features.menu.title: Out of the way
features.menu.text: Switch it on or off from the menu bar, hide the icon if you prefer, and let it open at login.
features.private.title: Private and open
features.private.text: No account, no tracking, no data collected. The whole source code is public, under the MIT license.
install.title: Install
requirements.title: Requirements
requirements.hardware: A MacBook with Apple silicon or an Intel processor.
requirements.admin: Administrator rights, once, to allow the background service that handles hibernation.
install.download_html: Download the .dmg file from the latest release.
install.copy_html: Open it and drag ClamStop onto Applications, then eject it.
install.open: Open ClamStop from the Applications folder. If macOS blocks it, follow the steps below.
install.service_html: Allow the background service: in System Settings > General > Login Items & Extensions (Login Items on macOS 14), turn the ClamStop switch on and authenticate.
gatekeeper.title: macOS blocks the app at first launch
gatekeeper.why: Builds that are not notarized by Apple are blocked at first launch; the release notes say whether a build is notarized. Only bypass this for a file downloaded from the ClamStop repository.
gatekeeper.step1_html: Open ClamStop once. In the warning, click Done (not “Move to Trash”).
gatekeeper.step2_html: Open System Settings > Privacy & Security and scroll down to Security.
gatekeeper.step3_html: Next to the message about ClamStop, click Open Anyway, then authenticate.
gatekeeper.step4_html: Confirm with Open Anyway in the last dialog.
gatekeeper.sonoma_html: On macOS 14 Sonoma, Control-click the app in Finder, choose Open, then Open again.
faq.title: Questions and answers
faq.clamshell.q: What if I want to work with the lid closed?
faq.clamshell.a: Turn “Sleep When the Lid Closes” off in the ClamStop menu: the lid then works as usual, clamshell mode included. Turn it on again whenever you like.
faq.wake.q: How do I wake the Mac?
faq.wake.a: Open the lid or press a key. After hibernation, waking up takes a few seconds longer because the memory is read back from disk.
faq.service.q: Why does ClamStop need a background service?
faq.service.a: Putting the Mac into hibernation requires administrator rights. A small background service does that part, and macOS asks you to approve it. It restores the default sleep settings when ClamStop is uninstalled.
faq.privacy.app: No. The app has no account, no analytics and no network code: nothing leaves your Mac.
faq.privacy.site: This website sets no cookies, runs no scripts and loads nothing from third parties. It is hosted on GitHub Pages, and GitHub logs the IP addresses of visitors for security purposes.
faq.source.a_html: Yes. The code is on GitHub under the MIT license. You can read it, build it yourself and contribute.
faq.uninstall.step1_html: Open the ClamStop settings (menu bar icon > Settings…, or open the app again from the Applications folder).
faq.uninstall.step2_html: Click Uninstall ClamStop…, then Uninstall. The default sleep settings are restored and the background service is removed.
faq.uninstall.step3: Move ClamStop from the Applications folder to the Trash.
faq.uninstall.more_html: App already deleted, or something went wrong? The uninstall guide covers it.
